<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915336_theRebbe_861" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915336_theRebbe_861__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that while the initial part of the maamar states war is only in the internal levels of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah, the later part details that war also exists in the level of Chayah, and true peace is only in Yechidah, analogous to Dovid's war and Shlomo's peace regarding the Temple.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And behold, in the aforementioned maamar of the Baal HaGeulah, at the beginning of the matter,</t>
    <t s="2">it is explained that the matter of the war</t>
    <t s="3">(of the Nefesh HaElokis with the Nefesh HaBahamis)</t>
    <t s="4">is in the Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah that are clothed in the body and the Nefesh HaBahamis,</t>
    <t s="5">but regarding the encompassing levels of Chayah and Yechidah, war does not apply.</t>
    <t s="6">However, afterwards, in the continuation of the maamar,</t>
    <t s="7">he explains in more detail that also in the aspect of Chayah there is the matter of war,</t>
    <t s="8">and the matter of peace is specifically in Yechidah.</t>
    <t s="9">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="10">that it is in the manner of what the Holy One, blessed be He, said to King Dovid</t>
    <t s="11">(when he wanted to build the Holy Temple)</t>
    <t s="12">"You have shed much blood..."</t>
    <t s="13">(and therefore)</t>
    <t s="14">"You shall not build a house for My Name... behold, a son will be born to you, he will be a man of rest... he will build a house for My Name..."</t>
    <t s="15">But nevertheless, the pattern of the Temple was made by Dovid</t>
    <t s="16">("The hand of Hashem was upon me, He made me understand"),</t>
    <t s="17">"And Dovid gave to Shlomo his son the pattern of the hall..."</t>
    <t s="18">And it needs to be understood,</t>
    <t s="19">since the Holy Temple is connected with rest</t>
    <t s="20">and peace specifically,</t>
    <t s="21">therefore it was said to Dovid, "You shall not build a house for My Name, for you are a man of wars,"</t>
    <t s="22">why were the preparations for the Holy Temple made by Dovid, who was a man of wars?</t>
    <t s="23">And the explanation of this can be said,</t>
    <t s="24">for then</t>
    <t s="25">(when Dovid wanted to build the Holy Temple,</t>
    <t s="26">and certainly when he prepared the pattern, etc.)</t>
    <t s="27">Dovid was in a state of rest,</t>
    <t s="28">and Hashem had given him rest from all his enemies around.</t>
    <t s="29">But since the rest of Dovid came through the wars he waged,</t>
    <t s="30">therefore the building of the Holy Temple had to be through Shlomo,</t>
    <t s="31">a man of rest,</t>
    <t s="32">rest in essence.</t>
    <t s="33">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="34">that this which is explained in the maamar</t>
    <t s="35">(at the beginning of the matter)</t>
    <t s="36">that also in the aspect of Chayah war does not apply, is in the manner of the rest of Dovid after he had conquered all the wars.</t>
    <t s="37">For in the aspects of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah that are clothed in the body and the Nefesh HaBahamis,</t>
    <t s="38">since the activity of the Nefesh HaElokis upon the Nefesh HaBahamis is in a manner of clothing and engagement,</t>
    <t s="39">for the perception of the animal soul is in the good of physical things,</t>
    <t s="40">and the G-dly soul engages with it to explain to it the good of G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="41">this is a matter of actual war.</t>
    <t s="42">But not so the aspect of Chayah,</t>
    <t s="43">since its activity upon the Nefesh HaBahamis is</t>
    <t s="44">(not in a manner of clothing, but)</t>
    <t s="45">that due to the revelation of the intensity of the will for G-dliness of the Nefesh HaElokis, the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis are automatically nullified,</t>
    <t s="46">this is not a matter of war.</t>
    <t s="47">And in general,</t>
    <t s="48">it is a matter of rest.</t>
    <t s="49">But this rest is</t>
    <t s="50">(not rest in essence,</t>
    <t s="51">but only)</t>
    <t s="52">due to the overpowering of the will of the Nefesh HaElokis,</t>
    <t s="53">analogous to the rest of Dovid after Hashem had given him rest from all his enemies,</t>
    <t s="54">that his rest was due to the fact that he had conquered all the wars.</t>
    <t s="55">But not so the nullification of the desires of the Nefesh HaBahamis through the revelation of the Yechidah, which is</t>
    <t s="56">(not that through the revelation of the Yechidah the nullification of desires is brought about,</t>
    <t s="57">but rather)</t>
    <t s="58">that from the perspective of the Yechidah</t>
    <t s="59">(for which there is no opposite, Heaven forbid)</t>
    <t s="60">there is no place from the outset for alien desires,</t>
    <t s="61">analogous to the rest of Shlomo,</t>
    <t s="62">which was</t>
    <t s="63">(not through conquest,</t>
    <t s="64">but)</t>
    <t s="65">rest in essence.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section details the different levels of service through war, explaining that the war in prayer is not a full war but a "sword of peace," while the primary war is during eating and especially in business dealings, which involves a "close combat" (krav) of embracing the opposing force.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And now, similar to this is the matter of the service that is through the path of war, which has many levels.</t>
    <t s="2">For the war in prayer,</t>
    <t s="3">"the time of prayer is a time of war,"</t>
    <t s="4">since during prayer he is abstracted from worldly matters and his engagement is to contemplate matters of G-dliness and to arouse love of Hashem and fear of Hashem,</t>
    <t s="5">but the contemplation</t>
    <t s="6">(and the love and fear)</t>
    <t s="7">must be in a way that is also grasped in the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis,</t>
    <t s="8">this is not an actual war</t>
    <t s="9">(and this is called a "sword"</t>
    <t s="10">of peace).</t>
    <t s="11">And the service through the path of war is primarily during eating and drinking,</t>
    <t s="12">"bread before the sword shall he eat,"</t>
    <t s="13">and similarly regarding other bodily needs.</t>
    <t s="14">And within this itself,</t>
    <t s="15">the primary war is during the engagement in business dealings,</t>
    <t s="16">commerce.</t>
    <t s="17">For the war of eating</t>
    <t s="18">(and similarly regarding other bodily needs)</t>
    <t s="19">is that his eating should be for the sake of Heaven and not to fulfill the desire of his soul,</t>
    <t s="20">meaning he fights against the lust and pleasure in the food</t>
    <t s="21">(and is not clothed in it),</t>
    <t s="22">but not so the engagement in business dealings, which must be</t>
    <t s="23">(according to Torah)</t>
    <t s="24">in a manner of clothing,</t>
    <t s="25">"your business dealings in faith."</t>
    <t s="26">[And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="27">that this is also the reason that all the clarifications are called by the name "Canaan,"</t>
    <t s="28">for the meaning of Canaan is merchant,</t>
    <t s="29">because the primary clarifications that are in a manner of clothing are in business dealings.]</t>
    <t s="30">And it follows,</t>
    <t s="31">that the war of eating is analogous to war with a sword</t>
    <t s="32">("bread before the sword shall he eat"),</t>
    <t s="33">for although the war of the sword is specifically when he is close to the enemy</t>
    <t s="34">(for this is the difference between a sword and a bow),</t>
    <t s="35">this closeness is only in place.</t>
    <t s="36">But not so the war in business dealings, which is analogous to the war called "krav," from the term closeness,</t>
    <t s="37">for the closeness of "krav" is</t>
    <t s="38">(not only in place,</t>
    <t s="39">but)</t>
    <t s="40">that the two combatants embrace each other,</t>
    <t s="41">as explained above</t>
    <t s="42">(section 2)</t>
    <t s="43">at length.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section concludes that through the service of "many are with me" which reveals the Yechidah, the redemption of the soul from the world, even in the close combat of business, is achieved in perfect peace, and even the sparks are redeemed and included in the Yechidah.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is "He redeemed my soul in peace from the battle against me,"</t>
    <t s="2">that even the service of clarifications that is in the manner of "krav" (close combat)</t>
    <t s="3">(and not only in the manner of war, but in the manner of "krav")</t>
    <t s="4">will be in a manner of "He redeemed in peace,"</t>
    <t s="5">peace with ultimate perfection, like the peace that was in the days of Shlomo,</t>
    <t s="6">and even higher—like the peace that will be in the future.</t>
    <t s="7">And the reason for this is as the continuation of the verse: "for many were with me."</t>
    <t s="8">For through the service of "many were with me,"</t>
    <t s="9">which is the arousal and revelation of the Yechidah, as explained at length in the aforementioned discourse of the Baal HaGeulah,</t>
    <t s="10">that each and every Jew has the power to arouse and reveal the Yechidah within him,</t>
    <t s="11">behold, through this is accomplished "He redeemed my soul in peace,"</t>
    <t s="12">the soul of the serving person,</t>
    <t s="13">for although he engages in worldly matters in order to clarify them in a manner of "krav,"</t>
    <t s="14">nevertheless, he will not be caught up in this, and his redemption will be in peace,</t>
    <t s="15">even to peace with ultimate perfection.</t>
    <t s="16">And furthermore, even the redemption of the sparks within worldly matters will be in peace,</t>
    <t s="17">"many were with me,"</t>
    <t s="18">that even the sparks that were initially in the aspect of "many"</t>
    <t s="19">(for they were in exile in the public domain, mountains of separation)</t>
    <t s="20">are included in the soul of the person who clarifies them,</t>
    <t s="21">"were with me,"</t>
    <t s="22">even to the point that they are included in the Yechidah within him.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
